title: Evaluate PR 4: package-json version mode (commit-time version bump)
description:
PR 4 (branch claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X) adds versionMode: "package-json" — a pre-commit hook that computes the next version and writes it into package.json, so the committed package.json always carries the real version. Goal (Justin): get the dynamic-version effect WITHOUT dynamic-version.local.json, which breaks CI (file is gitignored, remote envs must regenerate it) and breaks Expo EAS builds (which historically packed the repo without .git, making generation impossible). Target repos: eslint-config-jha-react-node, prompts — small, linear-history, low-ceremony.

Written ~2026-03 by Claude 4 Opus. Rebased onto main 2026-09-16 as local branch pr-4-package-json-mode (3 commits, one conflict in src/git-hooks-manager.ts resolved by keeping mains nonFatalSuffix and applying it to post-* hooks in both modes, deliberately NOT to pre-commit).
design:
VERDICT: the core idea is sound and worth keeping, but only for linear-history repos, and the implementation needs fixes before it is safe.

=== WHAT WORKS (verified by tests/integration/package-json-mode.test.ts, 16 tests) ===
- Sequential commits increment correctly in both calculation modes.
- Self-healing after --no-verify works exactly as designed: version set i commits ago yields +(i+1).
- The bumped version lands INSIDE the commit; working tree is left clean.
- package.json alone is sufficient for a consumer — no .git, no generated file. This is the goal of the PR and it is met.

=== VERIFIED BY TEST OR PROBE ===
1. npm STRIPS build metadata on publish. Probe: `npm publish --dry-run` on version 1.0.0+5 produced "publishprobe@1.0.0" and filename publishprobe-1.0.0.tgz. So append-commits — the DEFAULT calculation mode — makes every commit publish as the same version; the registry rejects the second. add-to-patch must be the default for this mode.
2. Unequal-length branches ALWAYS conflict on package.json (test). Equal-length branches are subtler and worse: both sides compute the SAME version, git auto-merges cleanly, and the merged result undercounts (two commits of work, one version) (test).
3. The design-doc claim "on the merge commit the pre-commit hook recalculates" is FALSE (test). git merge fires pre-merge-commit, not pre-commit; auto-merge commits keep a stale version.
4. git commit --amend re-runs pre-commit and double-bumps (test).
5. Rebase never re-runs the hook: the branch gains a commit while the version stands still (test).
6. The hook reads/writes the WORKING TREE package.json then `git add`s the whole file, so an unstaged half-finished package.json edit is silently swept into the commit (test). Data integrity, not just a `git add -p` annoyance.
7. updateLockfile() buys nothing. Probes: bun.lock records the root name but NOT the root version (grep: zero "version" keys), and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after a version-only bump exits 0; package-lock.json DOES record the root version but `npm ci` after a version-only bump also exits 0. `npm version X --no-git-tag-version --offline` updates both files instantly and offline if the drift is ever worth closing.
8. A failing package manager inside the hook is swallowed: a stub npm that exits 1 (proven invoked via a marker file) leaves the commit succeeding with no signal (test). "Failure is not empty" violation.

=== INFERRED FROM CODE READING, NOT DEMONSTRATED ===
9. stageFiles() also catches everything and only console.warn()s. If `git add` itself failed, package.json would be rewritten on disk but never staged, so the commit would record the OLD version while the tree shows the new one. I did not induce a git-add failure; this is a read of src/script-manager.ts, not an observation.
10. installCommand() calls generateVersionFile() (which creates version-manager.json with the default dynamic-file) BEFORE getVersionMode(), and no --mode flag exists — so a first install appears unable to produce package-json hooks; the user must install, hand-edit config, install again. Read from src/index.ts ordering; not executed end-to-end.
11. installGitHooks() only writes the current modes hooks and has no removal path, so switching package-json -> dynamic-file appears to leave pre-commit live forever. The leftover-file half IS covered by a test; that the leftover hook keeps bumping on later commits is inferred.
12. RESERVED_VERSION_NAMES gains "main" with no rationale anywhere in the diff or the plan. Observation, not a defect.

=== STYLE / RULES ===
- docs/plans/2026-03-27_committed-version-modes.md violates the current critical rules (beads replaced docs/plans/). Its content is preserved in this bead; the file should be deleted.
- calculatePreCommitVersion() duplicates its add-to-patch arithmetic three times.
- preCommitHandler(outputPath: string) is typed string but yargs supplies undefined (--output has no default); the ?? fallback is load-bearing while the type says it cannot fire.
acceptance_criteria: Justin has: (a) a clear verdict on whether the approach is worth keeping, (b) verified evidence for each claim rather than inference, (c) a prioritised list of what must change before it is safe to use, (d) automated tests that pin the behaviour so a future fix flips a documented expectation.
notes:
Test baseline verified, not inferred: main and the rebased branch BOTH fail the same 7 tests (5 watcher + 2 output-formatter snapshot). The PR introduces zero new failures and adds 20 passing unit tests; my 17 integration tests bring the branch to 124 pass / 7 fail.

The 23 failures seen on a first run are a SANDBOX artifact, not a defect: install shells out to `npm install --save-dev husky`, which EPERMs on ~/.npm/_cacache. With npm_config_cache redirected they pass. Not a code problem.

Pre-existing and unrelated: bun run lint fails on a stale artifact in .claude/worktrees/alternate-version-mode-wt/. Left alone.

Fixture harness notes: hooks must be committed (amended into the config commit) or they vanish on branch switch and every count shifts; node_modules/ must be gitignored in the fixture because the hooks npm install materialises it even in a dependency-free repo.

title: Default to add-to-patch in package-json mode (npm strips +N on publish)
notes: Closed 2026-09-16: Justin said "I do not currently publish almost anything to npm, so npm publish does not have to be a blocker." The finding stands (npm strips +N on publish, verified by npm publish --dry-run) but it is not a reason to change the default for him. If the branch-suffix idea (70i.10) lands, prerelease identifiers survive publish anyway, which makes this moot from a second direction.

title: Branch-name suffix in version when not on main (0.32.1-my-branch.3)
description:
Justins idea (2026-09-16): when not on the main branch, include the branch name in the computed version, e.g. 0.32.1-my-branch-name. He said it "seems potentially useful".

WHAT IT FIXES: the silent-collision case measured in 70i.8. Today two branches that add the SAME number of commits compute the IDENTICAL version, so git auto-merges the version field with no conflict and the merged result undercounts. A branch suffix makes the two sides structurally different, so that case becomes a visible conflict instead of a quiet wrong answer. Strict improvement in failure mode.

WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX: it does not reduce merge conflicts — it increases them. Both sides still rewrite the same line. Only a merge driver (70i.8) removes the conflict.

INDEPENDENT VALUE: a build labelled 0.32.1-my-branch.3 is identifiable on a device at a glance, which is close to the original reason version-manager exists.

SEMVER DETAIL: a hyphen suffix is a PRERELEASE, not build metadata. Precedence puts 0.32.1-foo BEFORE 0.32.1, which is semantically right — a branch build is a prerelease of the version it will become. Prerelease identifiers are also NOT stripped by npm publish, unlike the +N build metadata in 70i.1.

GOTCHA: semver prerelease identifiers allow only [0-9A-Za-z-] and dots. Real branch names contain slashes (claude/add-alternate-version-mode-Hnq9X), so the branch name must be sanitised, stably.

SUGGESTED SHAPE: 0.32.1-<sanitised-branch>.<n>, where n is the existing commit count. Sorts correctly, stays valid semver, reads well.
acceptance_criteria: Off by default behind a config knob (feature-knobs rule). Branch names containing slashes and other invalid characters produce valid semver. The main branch is unaffected. Tests cover sanitisation, that main is untouched, and that two equal-length branches no longer collide.

title: Stop writing dynamic-version.local.json in package-json mode
Pre-commit hook must read the INDEX, not the working tree
stageFiles/updateLockfile must fail loudly, not console.warn
Drop updateLockfile from the pre-commit hook (buys nothing)
Remove stale hooks when versionMode changes
Add --mode flag so a fresh install can reach package-json mode
Handle amend/rebase/merge in package-json mode (or document as linear-only)
description:
What actually happens on merges in package-json mode, measured 2026-09-16 (not inferred). Setup each time: base 0.1.0, feature +5 hooked commits -> 0.1.5, main +1 hooked commit -> 0.1.1.

- TRUE MERGE (--no-ff), diverged main: CONFLICTS on package.json. Resolve ours(main 0.1.1) -> merge commit lands at 0.1.2. The 5 feature commits are not counted.
- SQUASH MERGE, diverged main: CONFLICTS on package.json. Resolve ours -> 0.1.2. Resolve theirs(0.1.5) -> 0.1.6.
- SQUASH MERGE, main NOT diverged: no conflict, feature version 0.1.5 carries into the index, pre-commit adds 1 -> 0.1.6.

CONCLUSION: the outcome is decided entirely by which side of the version field wins the merge resolution; the pre-commit hook then adds exactly 1 on top. Both of the answers Justin floated are reachable and neither needs new algorithm work:
  - ours(main) => squash of a 500-commit branch lands at main+1 (his "could also just be 0.1.1")
  - theirs(branch) => lands at branch version +1 (his "0.1.500 is fine by me")

So a merge driver here is a POLICY choice, not a hard problem: it only has to pick a side for the version field and let normal JSON merging handle the rest of package.json.

IMPORTANT: this does NOT conflict with 70i.3 (read the index, not the working tree). In both merge flows the resolved version is STAGED, so reading the index yields the same answer as reading the working tree. Fixing 70i.3 does not change any merge outcome measured here.
design:
RECOMMENDED: merge driver that takes OURS (the branch being merged into) for the version field only, everything else normal JSON merge. Rationale: main version then counts commits landed ON MAIN, monotonic and stable regardless of how people branched; two 500-commit branches squash-merged do not produce wild jumps. Registered via .gitattributes (package.json merge=version-manager) plus a git config driver entry, both installable by the install command.

CAVEAT not yet verified: a merge driver is LOCAL git config, so it does not run for merges performed on GitHub servers (the merge/squash button). Server-side merges would still conflict and block the button. Needs checking before promising this fixes the PR workflow.
